claim: Nucleotide-sugar transporters (NSTs) are critical components of the cellular glycosylation machinery.
source: Nucleotide-sugar transporters (NSTs) are critical components of the cellular glycosylation machinery.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about NSTs' role in cellular processes.

claim: NSTs transport nucleotide-sugar conjugates into the Golgi lumen, where they are used for the glycosylation of proteins and lipids.
source: They transport nucleotide-sugar conjugates into the Golgi lumen, where they are used for the glycosylation of proteins and lipids
evidence: This describes the established function of NSTs based on prior research.

claim: NSTs subsequently transport the nucleotide monophosphate byproduct back to the cytoplasm.
source: they then subsequently transport the nucleotide monophosphate byproduct back to the cytoplasm
evidence: This describes the antiport function of NSTs, which is established knowledge.

claim: Dysregulation of human NSTs causes several debilitating diseases.
source: Dysregulation of human NSTs causes several debilitating diseases
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on genetic diseases caused by NST mutations.

claim: NSTs are virulence factors for many pathogens.
source: NSTs are virulence factors for many pathogens
evidence: This is supported by citations in the introduction discussing NSTs in parasites and fungi.

claim: This study presents the first crystal structures of a mammalian NST, the mouse CMP-sialic acid transporter (mCST), in complex with its physiological substrates CMP and CMP-sialic acid.
source: Here we present the first crystal structures of a mammalian NST, the mouse CMP-sialic acid transporter (mCST), in complex with its physiological substrates CMP and CMP-sialic acid.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the manuscript, supported by the crystallographic data presented.

claim: The structures provide detailed visualization of extensive protein-substrate interactions that explain the mechanisms governing substrate selectivity.
source: Detailed visualization of extensive protein-substrate interactions explains the mechanisms governing substrate selectivity.
evidence: This is supported by the structural data and analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Structural analysis of mCST's unique lumen-facing partially-occluded conformation reveals the concerted conformational transitions that occur during substrate transport.
source: Further structural analysis of mCST's unique lumen-facing partially-occluded conformation, coupled with the characterization of substrate-induced quenching of mCST's intrinsic tryptophan fluorescence, reveals the concerted conformational transitions that occur during substrate transport.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparisons and tryptophan fluorescence data.

claim: NSTs are products of the solute carrier 35 (SLC35) gene family in humans.
source: Nucleotide-sugar transporters (NSTs) are products of the solute carrier 35 (SLC35) gene family in humans and are a critical part of the glycosylation machinery in all eukaryotes (Hadley et al., 2014; Ishida and Kawakita, 2004; Song, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: NSTs are responsible for transporting nucleotide sugars from the cytoplasm, where they are synthesized, into the Golgi lumen where they are then utilized by glycosyltransferases to glycosylate proteins and lipids.
source: They are responsible for transporting nucleotide sugars from the cytoplasm, where they are synthesized, into the Golgi lumen where they are then utilized by glycosyltransferases to glycosylate proteins and lipids (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Capasso and Hirschberg, 1984; Milla and Hirschberg, 1989; Tiralongo et al., 2006; Waldman and Rudnick, 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in a figure.

claim: NSTs provide an essential role of transporting the nucleotide monophosphate (NMP) byproduct of the glycosyltransferase reaction back to the cytoplasm where it can be recycled.
source: NSTs provide an additional essential role of transporting the nucleotide monophosphate (NMP) byproduct of the glycosyltransferase reaction back to the cytoplasm where it can be recycled.
evidence: This describes the antiport function of NSTs, which is established knowledge.

claim: Many glycosyltransferases are inhibited by NMPs.
source: Since many glycosyltransferases are inhibited by NMPs, this antiport property of NSTs provides an additional layer of regulation of glycan synthesis (Hirschberg et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The antiport property of NSTs provides an additional layer of regulation of glycan synthesis.
source: Since many glycosyltransferases are inhibited by NMPs, this antiport property of NSTs provides an additional layer of regulation of glycan synthesis (Hirschberg et al., 1998).
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited knowledge about glycosyltransferase inhibition.

claim: Many NSTs are not obligatory antiporters.
source: Many NSTs are not obligatory antiporters, but the presence of NMPs in the lumen accelerates nucleotide sugar uptake several-fold through a poorly-understood process termed 'trans-stimulation' (Capasso and Hirschberg, 1984; Milla and Hirschberg, 1989; Tiralongo et al., 2006; Waldman and Rudnick, 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The presence of NMPs in the lumen accelerates nucleotide sugar uptake several-fold through a poorly-understood process termed 'trans-stimulation'.
source: Many NSTs are not obligatory antiporters, but the presence of NMPs in the lumen accelerates nucleotide sugar uptake several-fold through a poorly-understood process termed 'trans-stimulation' (Capasso and Hirschberg, 1984; Milla and Hirschberg, 1989; Tiralongo et al., 2006; Waldman and Rudnick, 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Glycosylation is the most common form of protein and lipid modification.
source: Glycosylation is the most common form of protein and lipid modification.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Glycosylation affects nearly every aspect of biology by modifying protein folding, stability, and functional properties.
source: It affects nearly every aspect of biology by modifying protein folding, stability, and functional properties (Dwek et al., 2002; Moremen et al., 2012; Ohtsubo and Marth, 2006; Stanley, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Glycans are typically terminated by sialic acids.
source: Glycans are typically terminated by sialic acids, which is important for many cell adhesion processes but also serves as ligands for pathogen invasion (Varki, 2008; Varki and Schauer, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Sialic acids are important for many cell adhesion processes and serve as ligands for pathogen invasion.
source: Glycans are typically terminated by sialic acids, which is important for many cell adhesion processes but also serves as ligands for pathogen invasion (Varki, 2008; Varki and Schauer, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: NST activity controls the concentrations of nucleotide sugars in the Golgi lumen.
source: Since NST activity controls the concentrations of nucleotide sugars in the Golgi lumen, disruption of NST activity can have many adverse physiological effects.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of NSTs.

claim: Disruption of NST activity can have many adverse physiological effects.
source: Since NST activity controls the concentrations of nucleotide sugars in the Golgi lumen, disruption of NST activity can have many adverse physiological effects.
evidence: This is an inference based on the role of NSTs and supported by subsequent discussion of genetic diseases.

claim: There are a number of genetic diseases caused by mutations in human NST genes that have severe and debilitating phenotypes.
source: There are a number of genetic diseases caused by mutations in human NST genes that have severe and debilitating phenotypes (Jaeken and Matthijs, 2007; Song, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Some NSTs are potently inhibited by antiviral nucleoside analogs.
source: In addition, some NSTs are potently inhibited by antiviral nucleoside analogs, which may form the basis for some of the side effects associated with this class of drugs (Chiaramonte et al., 2001; Hall et al., 1994).

claim: Altered glycosylation profiles of cell-surface proteins are a property of malignant cells.

source: Additionally, altered glycosylation profiles of cell-surface proteins are a property of malignant cells, and studies have shown that pharmacological block of some NSTs can inhibit tumor metastasis (Caffaro and Hirschberg, 2006; Esko and Bertozzi, 2009; Hadley et al., 2014; Ohtsubo and Marth, 2006; Song, 2013; Stowell et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

source: Mammals express seven NSTs, which collectively transport the eight nucleotide sugars used in Golgi glycan synthesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Each NST is highly selective for either one or two nucleotide sugars and the corresponding NMP.
source: Each NST is highly selective for either one or two nucleotide sugars and the corresponding NMP – a critical property that is required for the proper hierarchical assembly of glycans.

claim: NST selectivity is a critical property that is required for the proper hierarchical assembly of glycans.
source: Each NST is highly selective for either one or two nucleotide sugars and the corresponding NMP – a critical property that is required for the proper hierarchical assembly of glycans.

claim: Analysis of the mCST structures, coupled with functional characterization, elucidates the fundamental principles of the structure-function relationship of NSTs.
source: Analysis of these structures, coupled with functional characterization of mCST, elucidates the fundamental principles of the structure-function relationship of NSTs.

claim: mCST is 91% identical to human CST (hCST).

source: When mCST is purified in detergent, it retains saturatable substrate binding, with a Kd of 6.3 ± 1.2 µM and 482 ± 147 µM for CMP and CMP-Sia, respectively (Figure 1A).

source: Purified mCST also transports CMP-Sia when reconstituted into liposomes, with a Vmax of 6.5 ± 0.6 nmol/mol mCST/min and a Km of 58.1 ± 13.2 µM (Figure 1B and C), which is within the range of reported Km's for CMP-Sia transport for human or mouse CST expressed in Golgi (Aoki et al., 2003; Chiaramonte et al., 2001; Milla and Hirschberg, 1989; Tiralongo et al., 2006).

claim: The Km of mCST for CMP-Sia transport is within the range of reported Km's for CMP-Sia transport for human or mouse CST expressed in Golgi.

claim: A detailed model of mCST was built that refined to R/R-free factors of 24.1/25.2%.
source: We solved the structure of these crystals with molecular replacement using the model of full-length mCST as the search model, and built a detailed model of mCST that refined to R/R-free factors of 24.1/25.2% (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D, Table 2).

claim: The structure of mCST consists of a 10-TM bundle.

claim: The general topology of mCST resembles that seen in other members of the larger drug/metabolite transporter (DMT) superfamily.

claim: The 10-TM DMT proteins are thought to have arisen from an ancient helix addition to the 4-TM proteins followed by a gene duplication event.
